To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequency of the mucoid phenotype in P. aeruginosais isolates from cyst fibrosis (CF), a chronic lung infection of CF patients, is high, and that this phenotype is due primarily to mutations in the mucoid gene (mucA).

the mucA gene is the most likely locus for conversion to mucoidal phenotype of P. aeruginosain CF, and mucA mutations may contribute to the pathogenesis of P. aeruinosain CF by enhancing the resistance of the bacteria to the innate clearance mechanism of the lung.

(i) mucoid P. aeurginosa strains isolated from CF patients and other clinical sources have mucA mutations; (ii) the frequency of mucA mutations is 84% in the CF isolates; (iii) inactivation of mucA is the most frequent mechanism of conversion to the mucoid phenotype in CF; and (iv) mucoid Pseudomonad aeruginosa is more resistant to clearance from the lung than the corresponding nonmucoid strains
